chunks: Sulayman ibn Khalid asked Abu Abdullah عليه السلام:

About a man who closed his door on a bird and it died, so he عليه السلام said: "If he closed the door on it after entering iḥrām, then a sacrificial blood-offering is upon him; and if he closed it before entering iḥrām while he was in a halal state, then its price is upon him."

key_terms.أَحْرَمَ: entered the state of iḥrām for hajj or 'umrah
key_terms.ثَمَنُهُ: its monetary value, to be paid as compensation
key_terms.حَلَالٌ: being outside iḥrām in a permissible state
key_terms.دَمٌ: a sacrificial blood-offering due as compensation
key_terms.طَيْرٍ: a bird or game bird involved in the ruling

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a muhrim closes a door on a bird and it dies?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning liability for the death of a bird caused by confinement. It distinguishes between killing that occurs after entering iḥrām, which requires a damm, and before iḥrām in a halal state, which requires payment of the bird's value.
